title: How to tell constructive criticism from bad business advice: Franks vs. Gerrys
summary: Jason Cohen recounts nearly giving a "sales veteran" partner 50% of Smart Bear and renaming it, and uses dieting as an analogy: no advice is objectively right, only right for you and sustainable. He lists practical filters for judging advice (context match, questions over commands, measurable ideas, gut feel).

principles.text: Startup advice is contradictory; ask what works for this company and founder, not what is objectively best.
principles.quote: For every example that incontrovertibly proves "X is right," there's another equally compelling story of success where the mantra was "X is wrong."

principles.text: Advice must be sustainable for you; don't force yourself into channels you dislike and won't keep up.
principles.quote: if you think Twitter is insipid and Facebook is unserious and Instagram is fake, will you really be successful if you force yourself to post there?

principles.text: Advisors mostly give advice to themselves; trust it only if their goals, market, customers and competitors match yours.
principles.quote: The rule of thumb is: Advisors give advice to themselves.

principles.text: Good advisors ask pointed questions rather than issuing commands; be wary of axioms handed down as gospel.
principles.quote: Frank presented his view as a series of statements; axioms, even. Gerry couched his perspective as pointed questions that required either rebuttal or agreement.

principles.text: "This is how it's done" is neither a reason to follow nor to reject; investigate tradition like any other idea.
principles.quote: So, traditional answers carry neither positive nor negative baggage; they should be investigated like all other ideas.

principles.text: Prefer advice that comes with a way to measure success, so you can drop it if it doesn't work for you.
principles.quote: Does the advisor volunteer a clear way to measure the success of her new idea? If so, the idea is self-evaluating, and you can change if it happens to not work for you.
